# Review of the 20 hypotheses

**A key implementation detail.** In this setup (sklearn-style MLP), the L2 penalty is scaled by alpha divided by the minibatch size. Each step is also taken more often at small batch sizes. So the effective weight decay is much stronger with tiny batches. Learning rates of 0.278 and 1 with Adam usually diverge.

**Kept (12):**
- **#1 (LR↑ | width high, lower):** Wide nets diverge sooner at large Adam steps.
- **#3 (alpha↑ | batch low, lower):** Alpha/batch scaling makes L2 strongest at batches of 4 to 10.
- **#6 (LR↑ | batch low, lower):** Small batches already get many updates, so a higher LR mostly adds instability.
- **#7 (batch↑ | LR low, lower):** Step-count-limited training is hurt badly by fewer updates.
- **#8 (batch↑ | LR high, higher):** Larger batches stabilize near-divergent runs.
- **#9 (width↑ | LR high, lower):** Plausible.
- **#10 (depth↑ | LR low, lower):** Plausible.
- **#12 (alpha↑ | depth high, lower):** Plausible.
- **#13 (depth↑ | alpha high, lower):** Plausible.
- **#15 (LR↓ | batch high, lower):** Plausible.
- **#16 (width↑ | depth low, higher):** Plausible.
- **#18 (LR↑ | depth low, higher):** Plausible.

**Dropped (8):**
- **#2:** The direction is genuinely ambiguous.
- **#4:** It contradicts the per-batch L2 scaling. The effect should be *higher* at large batches, so I reversed it.
- **#5:** No clear mechanism.
- **#11:** Mild L2 under per-sample scaling barely matters at any width.
- **#14:** Weak; unregularized wide MLPs on tabular data rarely suffer.
- **#17:** Self-contradictory.
- **#19:** Vague.
- **#20:** Weak.

**Added (8):**
- alpha↑ | batch high, higher
- alpha↑ | alpha high, lower
- LR↑ | LR high, lower
- LR↓ | LR low, lower
- batch↑ | alpha high, higher
- depth↑ | LR high, lower
- width↑ | width low, higher
- LR↓ | batch low, higher
